messages.content: Get the latest closing prices and volumes for Apple Inc., Google LLC., and Microsoft Corporation in the New York Stock Exchange

function.name: get_stock_data
function.description: Retrieve the most recent trading day's closing price and volume for a specified stock. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

symbol.description: The stock symbol of the company.

data_points.description: The type of data you want to retrieve for the stock. This can include closing price, opening price, volume, etc.

message.reasoning:
The user wants the latest closing prices and volumes for Apple Inc., Google LLC., and Microsoft Corporation in the NYSE. Actually Apple (AAPL) is on NASDAQ, not NYSE. Google (Alphabet) is also on NASDAQ. Microsoft (MSFT) is on NASDAQ. But the user says "in the New York Stock Exchange". That might be a mistake; maybe they want the latest closing prices and volumes for those companies regardless of exchange. We should clarify or correct? The user explicitly asks for "Apple Inc., Google LLC., and Microsoft Corporation in the New York Stock Exchange". They might think those companies are listed on NYSE. We could politely point out that they are actually listed on NASDAQ. But we should follow instructions: "When responding to user requests, do not mention the policies." There's no policy violation. We can provide the data. We need to use the function get_stock_data. The function signature expects symbol and data_points: "price" | "volume"[].

We need to call the function for each symbol. Or we can combine? The function only accepts one symbol at a time. So we need to call it three times. Let's do that. We'll call get_stock_data with symbol "AAPL", data_points ["price", "volume"]. Then "GOOG" or "GOOGL"? Alphabet has two classes: GOOGL (Class A) and GOOG (Class C). Usually "GOOG" is used for the common ticker. We'll use "GOOG". Then "MSFT".

We'll produce separate calls.
